anya: ran a 4x precision sweep (FP16 / BF16 / INT8 / FP8 hybrid) on marlin-70b across US-WEST1, EU-WEST1, AP-SOUTHEAST1. posting top-level results and a few curiosities.

marcus: awesome — summary numbers?

anya: TL;DR: INT8 gives the best speedups on H100 (≈1.9x over FP16) but only ~1.3x on A100; FP8 on L4 is surprisingly good for latency-sensitive tails (2.2x over FP16) but has small QA quality delta on our SQuAD subset.

devin: can you drop the run commands + perf outputs?

anya: sure. below is the run command we used and the per-gpu P50 token lat / throughput (tokens/sec) for 2048 context, batch=4 generation workload.

```
# run used
run_bench --model marlin-70b --precision {fp16|bf16|int8|fp8} --gpu {h100,a100,l4} --region {us-west1,eu-west1,ap-southeast1} --batch-size 4 --ctx 2048 --seq 512
```

H100 (us-west1)
- FP16: p50_token = 11.8ms, throughput = 1,700 tok/s
- BF16: p50_token = 12.0ms, throughput = 1,650 tok/s
- INT8: p50_token = 6.2ms, throughput = 3,200 tok/s
- FP8: p50_token = 7.1ms, throughput = 2,850 tok/s

A100 (eu-west1)
- FP16: p50_token = 13.6ms, throughput = 1,450 tok/s
- BF16: p50_token = 13.9ms, throughput = 1,420 tok/s
- INT8: p50_token = 9.8ms, throughput = 1,900 tok/s
- FP8: p50_token = 10.1ms, throughput = 1,820 tok/s

L4 (ap-southeast1)
- FP16: p50_token = 18.5ms, throughput = 1,050 tok/s
- BF16: p50_token = 18.9ms, throughput = 1,020 tok/s
- INT8: p50_token = 10.4ms, throughput = 1,820 tok/s
- FP8: p50_token = 8.4ms, throughput = 2,300 tok/s

marcus: interesting that INT8 gains shrink on A100 — kernel selection? which attention kernel did you use?

anya: we used flash_attention v2 on H100 and A100 for FP16/BF16, switched to fused_gemm_kernels_v3 for INT8/FP8 where available. On L4 we used the nvtransformer fallback (no flash).

sophia: what about quality? any regressions on downstream evals?

anya: did exact evals on 3 datasets (SQuAD QA EM, TriviaQA F1, Code-synth correctness@1). numbers are deltas relative to FP16 baseline:

- INT8 (H100): SQuAD EM -0.4%, TriviaQA F1 -0.8%, Code-correctness -0.3%
- INT8 (A100): SQuAD EM -1.1%, TriviaQA F1 -1.5%, Code -0.9%
- FP8 (L4): SQuAD EM -1.9%, TriviaQA F1 -2.2%, Code -0.6%

devin: FP8 on L4 drop is bigger than I'd expect. Was this standard quantization or mixed-precision per-layer tuning?

anya: mixed: we applied per-channel symmetric quantization for weights + activation scaling with a small calibration set (1k example prompts). FP8 run was the default hybrid profile (outlier-aware mantissa scaling). We observed a few attention head saturation cases on FP8 for reasoning-heavy prompts.

marcus: sounds like tradeoff space: H100 + INT8 = best perf + tiny quality hit; A100 INT8 needs kernel work or different qprofile; L4 FP8 gives great latency but quality needs per-layer exceptions.

ci-bot: nightly-regression: marlin-70b-int8-h100 passed unit tests, SQuAD delta -0.45% (within threshold), perf-change +88% vs fp16. (ci link: https://ci.internal/redwood/bench/1967890123) :white_check_mark:

anya: next steps I'm proposing:
- open ticket to explore A100 INT8 kernel tuning (marcus + eng-runtime)
- add per-layer FP8 exception list for L4 and run 10k calibration prompts (devin + sofia)
- capacity sizing note: if customers switch marlin-70b from FP16 to INT8 on H100, conservatively expect ~1.7x throughput uplift in steady-state (we measured up to 1.9x on isolated runs). update cost model dashboard.

sophia: +1 on the per-layer exceptions. also let's add a small eval harness for long-context reasoning tasks — that's where FP8 had the worst regressions.

anya: i'll file the tickets and drop the raw CSVs and flame graphs to the eng-ml bench drive. quick link to the core perf CSV: https://drive.internal/redwood/eng-ml/bench/1967890123/results.csv

marcus: thanks, super actionable. i'll start A100 kernel experiments tomorrow and ping when I have a micro-benchmark. :rocket:

devin: added a note to the deploy playbook about fallback policies: if FP8/INT8 quality regresses >1% on critical evals, route to FP16 in the same region automatically.

anya: perfect. closing this thread — will update when tickets are ready. :lock:
